Question: A man buys a house for \(\$10{,}000\) and rents it. He puts \(12\dfrac12\%\) of each month’s rent aside for repairs and upkeep; pays \(\$325\) a year taxes and realizes \(5\dfrac12\%\) on his investment. The monthly rent is:
Solution:
Put all amounts on a yearly basis. The required annual profit after the repair allowance and taxes is
\[
0.055\cdot10{,}000=550\text{ dollars}.
\]
Reserving \(12\tfrac12\%\) of each month's rent also reserves that percentage of the year's rent. The remaining \(87\tfrac12\%=0.875\) must cover both the profit and the annual taxes, totaling
\[
550+325=875\text{ dollars}.
\]
Because \(875\) dollars is only \(87.5\%\) of the annual rent, divide by \(0.875\) to recover the whole:
\[
\text{annual rent}=\frac{875}{0.875}=1000\text{ dollars}.
\]
The monthly rent is therefore
\[
\frac{1000}{12}=\frac{250}{3}\approx83.33\text{ dollars}.
\]
Rounded to the nearest cent, the answer is \(\boxed{\$83.33}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
